cemc-cimc-2013-b3d.prompt:
The *positive difference list* (PDL) of a set of integers is a list, written in increasing order, of the positive differences between all possible pairs of integers in the set. For example, the set $\{2, 5, 12\}$ produces a PDL consisting of three integers 3, 7, 10 which are distinct, while the set $\{3, 4, 6, 9\}$ produces a PDL consisting of six integers 1, 2, 3, 3, 5, 6 which are not distinct.


(d) Prove that the PDL of every set of integers of the form $\{3, q, r, s, t\}$ with $3 < q < r < s < t$ and $t < 14$ contains repeated integers.
cemc-cimc-2013-b3d.answer: Distinct gaps would have to be exactly $1, 2, 3, 4$ (sum $\le 10$), and every arrangement creates a repeat: $1$ next to $2$ or $3$ gives $3$ or $4$ again; otherwise $1$ is only next to $4$ and $2, 3$ are adjacent, giving $1+4 = 2+3$.
